question.prompt:
Lakshmi has \(5\) round coins of diameter \(4\) centimeters. She arranges the coins in \(2\) rows on a table top, as shown below, and wraps an elastic band tightly around them. In centimeters, what will be the length of the band?

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The tightly wrapped band consists of straight portions between coins and curved portions along their edges. We can find these two total lengths separately.

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

Each coin has radius \(2\) centimeters. Join the centers of the four corner coins to form a trapezoid. Its bottom side spans two touching-coin gaps, so its length is \(2\cdot4=8\) centimeters. Its top side and its two slanted sides each join the centers of touching coins, so each has length \(4\) centimeters.

Each straight portion of the band has the same length as the corresponding side of this center trapezoid. To see why, draw the radii to the two points where that straight portion touches the coins. These radii are equal, parallel, and perpendicular to the band. Moving both centers along those radii by the same amount produces the two contact points, preserving the distance between them. Therefore, the straight portions total
\[
8+4+4+4=20\text{ centimeters}.
\]

The arcs round the four corners of the center trapezoid. The radii at the ends of each arc are perpendicular to the adjoining straight portions, so its central angle equals the exterior turn at that corner. These four exterior turns add to \(360^\circ\). Since all the arcs have radius \(2\), together they have the length of one complete circle:
\[
2\pi\cdot2=4\pi\text{ centimeters}.
\]
Adding the straight and curved portions gives \(\boxed{4\pi+20}\) centimeters, choice \(\text{C}\).
solutions.title: Separate straight portions and arcs
